glosses: A public official whose duty it is to administer the law, especially by presiding over trials and rendering judgments; a justice.

examples.text: The parts of a judge in hearing are four: to direct the evidence; to moderate length, repetition, or impertinency of speech; to recapitulate, select, and collate the material points of that which hath been said; and to give the rule or sentence.

glosses: A person who decides the fate of someone or something that has been called into question.
A person officiating at a sports event, a contest, or similar; referee.

examples.text: At a boxing match, the decision of the judges is final.

glosses: A person who evaluates something or forms an opinion.

examples.text: She is a good judge of wine.
They say he is a poor judge of character considering all the unreliable friends he has made.

glosses: A shophet, a temporary leader appointed in times of crisis in ancient Israel.
To sit in judgment on; to pass sentence on (a person or matter).

examples.text: A higher power will judge you after you are dead.

glosses: To sit in judgment, to act as judge.

examples.text: Justices in this country judge without appeal.

glosses: To judicially rule or determine.
To sentence to punishment, to judicially condemn.

examples.text: He was judged to die for his crimes.

glosses: To award judicially; to adjudge.
To form an opinion on; to appraise.

examples.text: I judge a man’s character by the cut of his suit.
Let us be judged for what we attempted rather than what we achieved.

glosses: To constitute a fitting appraisal or criterion of; to provide a basis for forming an opinion on.

examples.text:
Noble and milde this Perſean ſeemes to be,

glosses: To arbitrate; to pass opinion on something, especially to settle a dispute etc.

examples.text: We cannot both be right: you must judge between us.

glosses: To have as an opinion; to consider, suppose.

examples.text: I judge it safe to leave the house once again.

glosses: To form an opinion; to infer.

examples.text: I judge from the sky that it might rain later.
THE sun was up so high when I waked that I judged it was after eight o'clock.

glosses: To criticize or label another person or thing; to be judgmental toward.

examples.text:
There's something wrong with the world today; the light bulb's getting dim.
There's meltdown in the sky.
If you can judge a wise man by the color of his skin,
Mister, you're a better man than I

examples.text: Vous jugez cet homme trop sévèrement.

examples.text: Vous en jugez légèrement, témérairement. — Jugez favorablement de lui.

glosses: Conjecturer, estimer que, être d’avis, d’opinion que…

examples.text: La prière, c'est […] une sorte de tapage doublé de flagornerie. Ainsi en jugent […] les rationalistes qui affirment que rien n'est aussi absurde que de s'adresser à un Dieu immuable pour lui demander de bouleverser les lois de son univers en notre faveur.
Le système de raréfaction des naissances est ici tellement ancré dans les esprits, qu'il finit par être jugé comme le signe d'une vie raisonnable, ….
Le Prince […] ne peut naturellement vous recevoir en ce moment, mais il juge que votre venue est providentielle. Une dernière grâce du ciel, un heureux présage.
Nous serions alors préoccupés par les inégalités, que beaucoup jugent pernicieuses, plutôt que par la pauvreté absolue, que ces mêmes personnes et beaucoup d'autres jugent plus pernicieuse encore.

glosses: Évaluer ; estimer.

examples.text: Cependant, il juge assez correctement des distances et ne lance pas sa langue à l'étourdie sur une proie hors d'atteinte.
